prompt_text: Where should I stay in Branson Missouri, an Airbnb or a hotel, and which specific places are best?
answer_verbatim:
Short answer: it depends on what you want to do. Hotels are usually best if you want convenience, consistent service and on‑site amenities (pools, breakfast, front‑desk help, show shuttles). Airbnbs/cabins are best if you want more space, a kitchen, privacy and a lake or mountain feel. Tell me your dates, budget and who you’re traveling with and I’ll narrow choices — below are practical guidelines and solid options to consider.

When to pick which
- Hotel — if you want to be on/near the 76 “Strip,” close to shows, restaurants and attractions, or you want predictable service, daily housekeeping, pools and breakfast. Good for couples, older travelers, short stays, or people who don’t want to manage a private home.
- Airbnb/cabin — if you’re a family or group that wants separate bedrooms, a kitchen, outdoor space or a dock/lake access. Great for multi‑day lake trips, relaxing away from the crowds, or if you want space for kids to spread out.

Where to stay in Branson (neighborhoods)
- 76 Country Boulevard / “The Strip”: walkable to theaters, themed restaurants and attractions. Best for show-goers and first-time visitors.
- Branson Landing / Downtown Branson (on Lake Taneycomo): nicer shopping, riverwalk, restaurants, fountain shows; more relaxed than the Strip.
- Table Rock Lake / Hollister / Indian Point / Ridgedale: for lakefront cabins, boating, fishing — quieter and scenic.
- Near Silver Dollar City / Hwy 165 area: best if SDC is your main attraction (closer & less driving).
- Branson West / outskirts: often cheaper, more rural cabins and condos.

Recommended hotels (by type)
- Luxury / resort
  - Big Cedar Lodge (Ridgedale) — upscale lodges, great lake access, golf and resort amenities (excellent if you want a “resort” stay).
  - Chateau on the Lake Resort, Spa & Convention Center — lakefront, spa, fine dining.
- Mid‑range / family friendly
  - Hilton Promenade at Branson Landing — on the Landing with lake/riverwalk access; convenient for shopping/eating.
  - Drury Inn & Suites (Branson) — strong value, complimentary breakfast and evening social, good location for shows.
- Budget / reliable chains
  - Hampton Inn / Holiday Inn / Best Western properties on/near the Strip — consistent, comfortable, often good nightly rates.

Recommended Airbnb/cabin types and where to look
- Table Rock Lake waterfront cabin with private dock (Hollister, Indian Point, Kimberling City) — best for boating, fishing, sunsets.
- Log cabin in the Ozarks near Silver Dollar City — good for families wanting quick park access.
- Condo at Branson Landing (lakefront) — ideal for couples or small families who want walkable restaurants and entertainment.
- Large multi‑bedroom cabin with game room/firepit — good for reunions and groups.

How to choose a specific place
- If shows/Strip are your priority: pick a hotel on or very near 76 Country Boulevard (hotel convenience > Airbnb).
- If the lake or boating is your priority: choose a Table Rock Lake cabin (Airbnb/cabin rental).
- If you want balance (shops + theater + some quiet): Branson Landing condos or mid‑range hotels near downtown.
- Consider parking (many hotels have free parking; some condos/Airbnbs charge or limit parking), cancellation policy, and cleaning/house rules for rentals.

Booking tips
- Read recent reviews (last 6–12 months) for cleanliness and responsiveness.
- Check exact distance and drive times to the attractions you plan to use most.
- For cabins: confirm dock access, number of parking spots and if linens are provided.
- For hotels: ask about shuttle service to shows or breakfast/happy hour inclusions.

If you tell me: travel dates, how many people, your budget and whether you’ll be doing shows, Silver Dollar City, or lake activities, I’ll give 3–5 specific hotel and Airbnb listings (with pros and cons) tailored to your trip.
